stories.headline: Disfunción interoceptiva detectada antes de la depresión clínica
stories.finding: Se evaluó la interocepción (MAIA‑2) y los síntomas depresivos (PHQ‑9) en 431 sanos, 206 con depresión subclínica y 483 pacientes con MDD. Se encontró disfunción interoceptiva desde la fase preclínica, mayor deterioro en la clínica, escasa mejora con antidepresivos y capacidad predictiva de estas dimensiones sobre los síntomas, el pensamiento negativo.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la evaluación interoceptiva puede servir como marcador temprano y objetivo para identificar a personas en riesgo de desarrollar depresión clínica, orientando intervenciones preventivas antes de que los síntomas se consoliden.
stories.paperTitle: Unveiling the interoception impairment in various major depressive disorder stages
stories.originalAbstract: BACKGROUND: The intricate pathophysiological mechanisms of major depressive disorder (MDD) necessitate the development of comprehensive early indicators that reflect the complex interplay of emotional, physical, and cognitive factors. Despite its potential to fulfill these criteria, interoception remains underexplored in MDD. This study aimed to evaluate the potential of interoception in transforming MDD's clinical practices by examining interoception deficits across various MDD stages and analyzing their complex associations with the spectrum of depressive symptoms. METHODS: This study included 431 healthy individuals, 206 subclinical depression individuals, and 483 MDD patients. Depressive symptoms and interoception function were assessed using the PHQ-9 and MAIA-2, respectively. RESULTS: Interoception dysfunction occurred in the preclinical phase of MDD and further impaired in the clinical stage. Antidepressant therapies showed limited efficacy in improving interoception and might damage some dimensions. Interoceptive dimensions might predict depressive symptoms, primarily enhancing negative thinking patterns. The predictive model based on interoception was built with random split verification and demonstrated good discrimination and predictive performance in identifying MDD. CONCLUSIONS: Early alterations in the preclinical stage, multivariate associations with depressive symptoms, and good discrimination and predictive performance highlight the importance of interoception in MDD management, pointing to a paradigm shift in diagnostic and therapeutic approaches.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué el pensamiento negativo perpetúa la ansiedad sanitaria?
stories.headline: El pensamiento repetitivo explica sesgos de interpretación específicos en la ansiedad por la salud
stories.finding: En una muestra comunitaria de 124 personas con ansiedad sanitaria elevada, los participantes mostraron sesgos de interpretación específicos para estímulos que amenazan la salud, pero no para estímulos de ansiedad general, disforia o positivos. El pensamiento negativo repetitivo explicó parcialmente la relación entre estos sesgos y la ansiedad sanitaria.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que intervenir sobre la rumiación puede reducir los sesgos cognitivos que alimentan la ansiedad sanitaria, ofreciendo un objetivo terapéutico concreto para tratamientos cognitivo-conductuales.
stories.paperTitle: Specificity of computationally modeled interpretation biases in health anxiety and the contributions of repetitive negative thinking in a community sample of individuals with elevated health anxiety
stories.originalAbstract: Cognitive-behavioral models of health anxiety suggest interpretation biases for ambiguous information play a role in its etiology. This study sought to clarify how specific these biases are in health anxiety and how other potential causal processes, like repetitive negative thinking (RNT), are associated with interpretation biases and health anxiety. Participants from the community (N = 124) with at least mildly elevated levels of health anxiety (Short Health Anxiety Inventory scores ≥ 18) completed a self-report questionnaire assessing repetitive negative thinking (RNT), as well as an interpretation bias task based on the Word Sentence Association paradigm. Task outcomes were computationally modelled using drift diffusion modeling and interpretation bias was operationalized as drift rate, i.e., the rate of evidence accumulation to decide between two choices (in this case, the emotional interpretation or the benign interpretation). Results showed that individuals with health anxiety exhibit interpretation biases specific to health-threatening stimuli but not general anxiety, dysphoric, or positive stimuli. In addition, RNT partially explained the association between interpretation biases for health anxiety-related stimuli and health anxiety symptom severity. Our work suggests health anxiety-specific interpretation biases and repetitive negative thinking may be important targets for intervention, whether through psychotherapy or computerized interventions (e.g., cognitive bias modification).

stories.hook: ¿Por qué la incertidumbre no frena la extinción del miedo?
stories.headline: Intolerancia a la incertidumbre no afecta el aprendizaje de extinción
stories.finding: El estudio empírico con 101 estudiantes utilizó un procedimiento de condicionamiento de amenaza de dos días para examinar la relación entre la intolerancia a la incertidumbre (IU) y el aprendizaje de extinción, controlando medidas diagnósticas. Los resultados mostraron una asociación nula entre IU y la extinción del miedo.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la IU podría no ser un obstáculo central en la eficacia de terapias de exposición, lo que orienta a los clínicos a focalizar otros factores para mejorar la remisión en trastornos de ansiedad.
stories.paperTitle: Threat conditioning in anxiety-related disorders: an empirical study and systematic review
stories.originalAbstract: Anxiety disorders (AD) are a prevalent form of psychological disorder with far-ranging negative consequences for those suffering with them. Recent efforts have utilised human threat conditioning procedures to gain further understanding of how individuals with ADs respond to conditioned threat and safety cues. Research in this area is at the vanguard of optimising exposure-based treatments and recent developments have yielded promising results. Yet, exposure-based treatments are still marred with lower-than-desired remission rates and higher-than-desired relapse rates, hence further investigation of the factors that may inhibit the success of exposure-based therapies is needed. In chapter two, the reader will be introduced to the concept of intolerance of uncertainty (IU) and its suspected role in inhibiting extinction learning which has potential clinical implications. The empirical study within this chapter describes a two-day threat conditioning procedure using a student sample (N=101) with the aim of investigating the relationship between IU and extinction learning whilst controlling for diagnostic measures. The results demonstrate a null association between these two variables contradicting previous findings. In chapter three, the reader will be introduced to the relevant literature regarding threat conditioning and extinction processes in those with ADs. Although ADs and other specific anxiety-related conditions have had recent systematic reviews on this topic, there is a lack of synthesis in relation to panic disorder (PD) and specific phobia (SP). Hence, a systematic review was carried out focussing on patient-control differences in threat conditioning processes in relation to both PD and SP separately. The review uncovered interesting, yet tentative, patterns of results which indicate key patient-control alterations in threat acquisition in PD patients, and alterations in threat acquisition and extinction in SP patients. The results of both studies have meaningful clinical and academic implications which are outlined and discussed further.

stories.hook: ¿Los latidos monaurales pueden empeorar la ansiedad?
stories.headline: Latidos monaurales de alta intensidad reducen la eficacia ansiolítica de la música
stories.finding: En 207 participantes, los beats monaurales de baja y moderada intensidad redujeron la ansiedad más que la música sin beats (p=0.047, β=−0.46). En cambio, la mezcla de alta intensidad disminuyó la ansiedad menos que la música sola (p=0.047, β=0.42).
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la saliencia del ritmo influye en los efectos ansiolíticos, por lo que las intervenciones auditivas deben calibrar cuidadosamente la intensidad de los beats para maximizar el beneficio clínico.
stories.paperTitle: Music with monaural beats for anxiety reduction and mood enhancement in individuals with moderate trait-anxiety
stories.originalAbstract: Monaural beats embedded in music are a popular anxiety-relief intervention, yet implementation parameters and efficacy remain poorly understood. Across two studies of online participants with moderate trait anxiety, we tested whether theta-frequency (4–7 Hz) monaural beats in music produce anxiolytic and mood-enhancing effects beyond the same music alone, whether the salience of the beats relative to the music influences effects, and whether the effect of beats generalizes across heterogeneous musical stimuli. State anxiety, valence and arousal were measured before and after a 25-min listening period. In Study 1, participants ( N = 207) were randomly assigned to hear music without beats (Music-Only control) or the same piece with monaural beats blended at three different salience levels: Low-, Moderate-, or High-Beatmix. The Low- and Moderate-Beatmix conditions yielded greater anxiety reductions than Music-Only ( p adjusted = 0.047, β = −0.46, and p adjusted = 0.047, β = −0.46 respectively), whereas Music-Only reduced anxiety more than the High-Beatmix condition ( p adjusted = 0.047, β = 0.42), indicating that overly salient beats might disrupt anxiolytic effects. Time × Condition interactions were not significant for valence or arousal. In Study 2, participants ( N = 259) were randomized to one of four stylistically varied tracks, with or without beats at the Moderate-Beatmix level. Averaged across tracks, Beatmix conditions produced greater anxiety reductions ( p < 0.0001, β = −0.49) and positive-valence increases ( p = 0.029, β = 0.28) than Music-Only. As in Study 1, the Time × Condition interaction was nonsignificant for arousal. These studies provide some of the first evidence that adding monaural beats to music has anxiolytic effects beyond music alone, that efficacy depends on relative beat salience, and that findings replicate across a range of musical tracks.

stories.hook: ¿Los traumas infantiles alteran la percepción de seguridad?
stories.headline: Los ACE predicen menor neurocepción de seguridad psicológica en adultos
stories.finding: En una muestra de 222 adultos, los puntajes en la escala de Experiencias Adversas en la Infancia (ACE) se asociaron significativamente con una menor puntuación en la Escala de Neurocepción de Seguridad Psicológica (NPSS). Este hallazgo sugiere que los traumas tempranos influyen en la capacidad de percibir entornos como seguros.
stories.takeaway: Comprender que los traumas infantiles disminuyen la percepción de seguridad puede guiar intervenciones que fortalezcan la neurocepción, mejorando la prevención de trastornos de ansiedad y facilitando entornos terapéuticos más seguros.
stories.paperTitle: Unraveling the Nexus: Investigating the Relationship between Neuroception of Psychological Safety and Childhood Traumas
stories.originalAbstract: This research aims to explore the intricate relationships among neuroception of psychological safety and childhood traumas. Early life experiences, particularly adverse childhood experiences (ACEs), have been shown to impact neurodevelopment and influence later perceptions of psychological safety. This study seeks to build on existing literature by examining these intricate relationships. Analytical cross-sectional design was used to assess the participants at a single point in time. The data gathered throughout Lahore, Punjab from Jan 2024 to July 2024. The sample size of 222 adult participants was selected by the convenience sampling strategy. A diverse sample of adult’s age range of 20 and over recruited to ensure representation of various adult stages, genders, and cultural backgrounds. Assessment of participants was based on established measures and their eligibility for the study was determined accordingly. For assessment purpose three scales were used; Neuroception of Psychological Safety Scale (NPSS) for psychological safety and Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACE) for childhood trauma were used. Adverse childhood experiences measured by ACE to be a significant predictor of neuroception of psychological safety (p<.000) and also significant predictor of all its subscales of social engagement (p<.000), compassion (p<.000) and bodily sensations (p<.000). The results are in line with previous literature linking trauma with Polyvagal theory that Adverse childhood Experiences (ACEs) like violence, physical, emotional and sexual abuse, or being developed with such parents and other family members suffering from the mental health issues or substance abuse history can provide the base for physiological and mental health problems in later life.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la terapia centrada en la transferencia reducir síntomas borderline?
stories.headline: La psicoterapia focalizada en la transferencia reduce síntomas borderline en internado
stories.finding: En un estudio prospectivo con 74 pacientes con trastorno límite de la personalidad, 31 completaron seis meses de psicoterapia focalizada en la transferencia, reduciendo significativamente los síntomas (BSL‑23) con un efecto medio (d = 0,54). El grupo de lista de espera (27) no cambió.
stories.takeaway: Demuestra que la TFP en contexto de internado es una intervención eficaz para disminuir síntomas borderline, ofreciendo una alternativa basada en evidencia para tratamientos intensivos y subrayando la relevancia de la duración terapéutica.
stories.paperTitle: Transference-focused psychotherapy in an inpatient setting for borderline personality disorders: changes in symptomatology
stories.journal: Research in Psychotherapy Psychopathology Process and Outcome
stories.originalAbstract: This prospective, naturalistic, longitudinal study examined changes in borderline-specific symptoms in a six-month, manual-based transference-focused psychotherapy (TFP) inpatient treatment for patients with borderline personality disorder (BPD) in comparison to a waitlist control group. Seventy-four patients with BPD received TFP in a multi-professional inpatient setting, of whom 27 patients represented the waitlist control group. Thirty-one patients completed six months of treatment. Borderline-specific symptoms were measured by means of the Borderline Symptom List (BSL-23) prior to treatment (waitlist control group), at the beginning, after 3 months, and at the end of it. BSL-23 scores decreased significantly from the beginning to the end of the six-month inpatient therapy program with a medium effect size of d=0.54. There was no change in symptoms for the waitlist control group. Our findings suggest that inpatient TFP is effective in terms of the reduction of borderline-specific symptoms. In terms of this, the duration of the treatment seems to be a meaningful factor. Further research will investigate changes in specific psychodynamic aspects as well as in the follow-up measurement.

stories.headline: Determinantes de la vergüenza interna revelados en 906 adultos
stories.finding: En una muestra de 906 participantes de Irán, el modelo de regresión de contracción explicable permitió explorar la relación entre la vergüenza interna y variables como la competencia emocional, el trauma infantil, la alexitimia, la flexibilidad cognitiva y la tolerancia al malestar, revelando patrones diferenciados de contribución. Los resultados sugieren que estos factores pueden ser objetivos relevantes para intervenciones clínicas dirigidas a reducir la vergüenza interna.
stories.takeaway: Comprender los factores que alimentan la vergüenza interna orienta la evaluación y el diseño de tratamientos psicológicos personalizados, mejorando la eficacia terapéutica en trastornos donde la autocrítica es central.
stories.paperTitle: Comparing Linear Regression to Shrinkage Regression Algorithms using Python: A case study of Internal Shame
stories.originalAbstract: Purpose: Internal shame (IS) is a deeply distressing emotional state characterised by avoidance tendencies, diminished self-esteem, and negative self-perception, often accompanied by self-critical thoughts such as self-loathing. It significantly influences an individual's cognitive and emotional processes, shaping self-evaluation and overall functioning. Recent studies have highlighted its prominence as a construct with multifaceted psychological implications, impacted by various psychosocial and emotional factors. This study focuses on examining the determinants of internal shame, including emotional competency, childhood trauma, alexithymia, cognitive flexibility, and distress tolerance, utilising the Explainable Shrinkage Regression Model. Method: A total of 906 participants (53.1% female and 46.9% male) residing in Tehran were recruited in 2023 through convenience sampling on online platforms. The survey encompassed demographic variables (age and gender) and psychological assessments, such as measures of childhood trauma, social-emotional competence, internal shame, cognitive flexibility, and distress tolerance. Data analysis employed regression techniques, including Linear Regression, Ridge Regression, Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO), and Elastic Net Shrinkage Regression models. The independent variables included five features: childhood trauma, social-emotional competence, alexithymia, cognitive flexibility, and distress tolerance. The dependent variable was internal shame. Results: The results indicated that while each model presents its own advantages, Elastic Net regression showed marginally the best performance in prediction of IS having the lowest MSE and highest R2.

stories.hook: ¿El sueño actúa como puente entre estrés y bienestar laboral?
stories.headline: El sueño intermedia la relación entre estrés de adaptación y bienestar laboral en trabajadores filipinos.
stories.finding: El modelo de ruta mostró que la calidad del sueño mediaba la relación entre el estrés de adaptación y el compromiso con el ejercicio, y que ambos factores influían en el bienestar laboral. El modelo explicó el 22,5 % de la variabilidad del bienestar.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo destaca la importancia de mejorar la calidad del sueño como estrategia para reducir el estrés de adaptación y potenciar el bienestar laboral, ofreciendo una intervención focalizada que puede ser implementada en programas de salud ocupacional.
stories.paperTitle: Path Model of Well-Being Among Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) in Taiwan
stories.journal: Psychology and Education A Multidisciplinary Journal
stories.originalAbstract: This study examined the relationships among sleep quality, acculturative stress, commitment to exercise, and employee well-being among Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) in the manufacturing industry in Taiwan and identified the best-fitting path model of well-being. Using a quantitative descriptive-correlational design, data were collected from 234 OFWs through standardized questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson product-moment correlation, and path analysis with robust maximum likelihood estimation and bootstrapping. Findings showed low levels of sleep difficulties and acculturative stress, moderate commitment to exercise, and high employee well-being. Sleep quality was significantly related to acculturative stress, commitment to exercise, and well-being. Acculturative stress was also significantly related to commitment to exercise and well-being, whereas commitment to exercise and well-being were not significantly related at the bivariate level. The final path model demonstrated excellent fit and established sleep quality as the intervening variable connecting acculturative stress and commitment to exercise with well-being. The model explained 22.5% of the variance in sleep quality and 14.8% of the variance in well-being, with all structural paths statistically significant. The findings indicate that OFW well-being is multidimensional and shaped by interconnected psychosocial, behavioral, and sleep-related factors. Sleep quality emerged as a particularly important pathway linking cultural adjustment and exercise commitment to well-being. The study highlights the value of integrated workplace strategies addressing sleep, cultural adjustment, exercise, and employee well-being while recognizing that additional personal, occupational, and environmental factors contribute to well-being. Future research should examine protective and contextual factors and use longitudinal designs to clarify relationships and mechanisms.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la compasión grupal transformar trastornos de personalidad?
stories.headline: Intervención grupal basada en compasión mejora bienestar y reduce estrés en trastornos de personalidad
stories.finding: Los 16 participantes describieron que la intervención les motivó a restaurar el funcionamiento diario y, tras completarla, experimentaron una visión más positiva, mayor conciencia emocional, autocompasión, sentido de agencia y reducción del estrés. Identificaron como motores del cambio la conexión grupal, el enfoque en fortalezas y la experiencia compartida.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que los grupos basados en compasión pueden ser una herramienta eficaz para potenciar el bienestar y disminuir el estrés en pacientes con trastorno de personalidad, ofreciendo un enfoque complementario a la terapia tradicional centrada en síntomas.
stories.paperTitle: ‘I Realised I Have to Do It Myself’: Experiences of Clients With Personality Disorders in a Compassion‐Based Positive Psychology Group Intervention
stories.originalAbstract: Objective Effective treatment of personality disorders (PDs) should target not only symptom reduction but also the enhancement of mental well‐being. Compassion‐Based Positive Psychology Group Intervention (CB‐PPGI) has shown promising effects in other clinical populations, yet little is known about how individuals with PDs experience this intervention. This qualitative study explored participants' motivations for engaging in CB‐PPGI, experienced benefits, perceived mechanisms of change and facilitators and barriers to intervention success. Methods Semi‐structured interviews were conducted with 16 participants (12 completers, 4 non‐completers) who received CB‐PPGI while awaiting specialised treatment for PDs. Data were analysed using Reflexive Content Analysis. Results Participants were motivated by a desire to restore daily functioning, balance and self‐control. Experienced benefits included a more positive outlook, greater emotional awareness, increased self‐kindness, stronger personal agency, a greater sense of shared humanity, improved balance between activity and rest and reduced stress. Perceived mechanisms of change included group connection, a strengths‐based focus, experiential learning, acceptance and self‐compassion, emotional depth without pressure and a sense of safety fostered by therapist presence. Facilitators and barriers to intervention success included readiness for change, timing, motivation, group composition, trust, resilience and cognitive resources. Conclusion Participants experienced CB‐PPGI as supportive in strengthening agency, emotional awareness, self‐kindness and mental well‐being. These findings suggest that CB‐PPGI may complement established PD treatments by fostering recovery‐oriented and well‐being‐related processes alongside symptom‐focused therapeutic goals.
stories.abstract: Objective Effective treatment of personality disorders (PDs) should target not only symptom reduction but also the enhancement of mental well‐being. Compassion‐Based Positive Psychology Group Intervention (CB‐PPGI) has shown promising effects in other clinical populations, yet little is known about how individuals with PDs experience this intervention. This qualitative study explored participants' motivations for engaging in CB‐PPGI, experienced benefits, perceived mechanisms of change and facilitators and barriers to intervention success. Methods Semi‐structured interviews were conducted with 16 participants (12 completers, 4 non‐completers) who received CB‐PPGI while awaiting specialised treatment for PDs. Data were analysed using Reflexive Content Analysis. Results Participants were motivated by a desire to restore daily functioning, balance and self‐control. Experienced benefits included a more positive outlook, greater emotional awareness, increased self‐kindness, stronger personal agency, a greater sense of shared humanity, improved balance between activity and rest and reduced stress. Perceived mechanisms of change included group connection, a strengths‐based focus, experiential learning, acceptance and self‐compassion, emotional depth without pressure and a sense of safety fostered by therapist presence. Facilitators and barriers to intervention success included readiness for change, timing, motivation, group composition, trust, resilience and cognitive resources. Conclusion Participants experienced CB‐PPGI as supportive in strengthening agency, emotional awareness, self‐kindness and mental well‐being. These findings suggest that CB‐PPGI may complement established PD treatments by fostering recovery‐oriented and well‐being‐related processes alongside symptom‐focused therapeutic goals.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué el impostor aumenta el burnout académico?
stories.headline: Los sentimientos de impostor predicen el burnout académico, sin moderación de la narcisismo
stories.finding: Los análisis de moderación mostraron que los sentimientos de impostor predijeron significativamente el burnout académico en 300 estudiantes universitarios. Ni el narcisismo vulnerable ni el grandioso moderaron esa relación; sin embargo, el narcisismo vulnerable predijo directamente el burnout y sus subescalas, y el narcisismo grandioso solo la cinismo.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que intervenir directamente sobre los sentimientos de impostor y la vulnerabilidad narcisista puede prevenir el desgaste académico, más que enfocarse en la forma narcisista de la personalidad.
stories.paperTitle: The Relationship Between Impostor Feelings and Academic Burnout: The Moderating Role of Vulnerable and Grandiose Narcissism
stories.originalAbstract: Academic burnout is prevalent among university students and has been consistently linked to impostor feelings, yet the role of personality traits remains largely unexplored. Specifically, grandiose and vulnerable narcissism have not yet been examined in the impostor–burnout link. This study investigated whether vulnerable and grandiose narcissism moderate the relationship between impostor feelings and academic burnout, including its subscales (emotional exhaustion, cynicism, and reduced academic efficacy). Self-report data were obtained from 300 bachelor’s and master’s students in the Netherlands (Mage = 22.84 years, SD = 2.29). Moderation analyses were conducted to test the proposed relationships. The results showed that impostor feelings significantly predicted academic burnout. However, neither vulnerable nor grandiose narcissism moderated this relationship, either for overall burnout or across subscales. Notably, vulnerable narcissism was a significant direct predictor of overall burnout and its subscales, whereas grandiose narcissism significantly predicted cynicism only. Thus, vulnerable narcissism was associated with academic burnout, rather than moderating the impostor–burnout relationship. This highlights the importance of raising awareness of vulnerable narcissism and impostor feelings among student counselors for burnout prevention. Future research with larger, more adequately powered samples is needed to further investigate the moderating role of narcissism.

stories.hook: ¿Cómo afecta el trauma vicario al cuidado de salud?
stories.headline: El trauma vicario reduce significativamente la calidad del servicio de enfermería
stories.finding: En un estudio mixto con 174 enfermeras de Kenia, se encontró que los efectos emocionales del trauma vicario, entre los que se incluyen agotamiento emocional y burnout, se relacionan negativamente con la prestación de servicios de salud (r = -0.546). El análisis de regresión confirmó que mayores efectos emocionales predicen una disminución de la calidad del servicio.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo alerta a los gestores de salud sobre la necesidad de intervenir en el trauma vicario para preservar la calidad asistencial y la salud mental del personal.
stories.paperTitle: Emotional Effects of Vicarious Trauma on Health Care Services Delivered Among Nurses at AGC Tenwek Hospital in Bomet County, Kenya.
stories.journal: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
stories.originalAbstract: Vicarious trauma can affect nurses’ emotional wellbeing and their capacity to deliver quality healthcare services. This study examined the relationship between the emotional effects of vicarious trauma and healthcare service delivery among nurses at AGC Tenwek Hospital in Bomet County, Kenya. Guided by Constructivist Self-Development Theory and Resilience Theory, the study adopted a mixed-methods approach involving 174 nurses drawn from a target population of 307 registered nurses. Quantitative data were collected using structured questionnaires, while qualitative data were obtained through semi-structured interviews. Quantitative data were analysed using SPSS version 28, with descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and multiple linear regression, while qualitative data were analysed thematically. The findings revealed that nurses experienced emotional effects associated with exposure to patients’ traumatic clinical experiences, including emotional exhaustion, guilt, anxiety and burnout. Pearson correlation analysis indicated a negative relationship between emotional effects of vicarious trauma and healthcare service delivery (r=-0.546). Regression analysis further showed that emotional effects had a negative and statistically significant association with healthcare service delivery (B=-0.234, β=-0.203, p=0.010), after accounting for other predictors in the model. These findings suggest that greater emotional distress among nurses is associated with poorer perceived healthcare service delivery. The study recommends that AGC Tenwek Hospital strengthen staff counselling, psychological support, peer-support systems and resilience-building programmes to promote nurses’ emotional wellbeing and sustain compassionate, quality healthcare delivery.

stories.hook: ¿Qué predice mejor el divorcio a 12 años?
stories.headline: Predictores individuales, de pareja y socioeconómicos explican el divorcio a largo plazo
stories.finding: En una cohorte prospectiva de 368 parejas recién casadas, el 39 % se divorció en los 12 años siguientes. Los modelos estructurales bayesianos mostraron que los predictores individuales, la satisfacción conyugal, el comportamiento adaptativo de la pareja y el riesgo socioeconómico explicaron significativamente la probabilidad de divorcio.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que las intervenciones preventivas deben ir más allá de la comunicación de pareja, incorporando la evaluación de vulnerabilidades personales y contextos socioeconómicos para identificar parejas en riesgo y diseñar apoyos más integrales.
stories.paperTitle: Individual, interpersonal, and socioeconomic predictors of divorce: A 12-year prospective study.
stories.journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
stories.originalAbstract: Divorce is among the most common and costly life disruptions adults may face. Maladaptive and ineffective couple communication is routinely implicated in leading models as the cause of divorce, and interventions designed to prevent divorce accordingly prioritize changes in couple interaction patterns. Yet research linking couple communication to divorce has been inconsistent, and failures of communication-based interventions highlight the need for an expanded view of early signs of risk. Alternative perspectives on divorce draw attention to the vulnerabilities individuals bring into marriage and the socioeconomic circumstances couples must navigate once married, yet the predictive power of these perspectives has never been directly compared to the behavioral model. The current analyses address this gap through a study of 368 different-sex newlywed couples who provided data on six clusters of predictors within 6 months of marriage: relationship satisfaction for each spouse, individual vulnerabilities for each spouse, couples' adaptive behavior, and socioeconomic risk. Over the next 12 years, 39% of couples divorced. Preregistered Bayesian structural equation models and survival analyses demonstrated that each baseline risk factor independently predicted divorce in the expected direction. When all predictors were included simultaneously, only wives' individual vulnerabilities predicted divorce. Adaptive communication behaviors attenuated the risk conferred by wives' vulnerabilities. The best performing model explained 34% of variance in divorce, suggesting that at least one third of couples' divorce risk is detectable early in marriage. Exploring vulnerabilities and their effects promises to deepen understanding of how relationships develop and deteriorate and can clarify boundary conditions of behavioral models of divorce. stories.hook: ¿Las redes sociales fomentan la ayuda real entre jóvenes?
stories.headline: Revisión sistemática muestra influencia de redes sociales en conducta prosocial real
stories.finding: La revisión sistemática identificó estudios que observaron la conducta prosocial de adultos emergentes en contextos reales, descartando cuestionarios autoinformados y juegos económicos. Los hallazgos sugieren que factores de redes sociales pueden modular la ayuda real, aunque la evidencia aún es limitada.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo alerta a investigadores y profesionales sobre la necesidad de medir la prosocialidad en entornos naturales y considerar el papel de las plataformas digitales al diseñar intervenciones que promuevan la cooperación entre jóvenes.
stories.paperTitle: Social Media Influence on Emerging Adults’ Prosocial Behavior: A Systematic Review
stories.originalAbstract: Current literature has provided substantial empirical evidence on how different types of factors influence prosocial behavior, but limited literature explores the relationship between online social media factors and their psychological influence on emerging adults’ prosocial behavior. Moreover, the majority of experimental investigations have utilized self-reported questionnaires or irrelevant economic games to reflect people’s prosocial behavior instead of measuring prosocial behavior demonstrated in real-life, natural settings. Considering the gaps in past research, this systematic review aims to identify literature regarding the influence of social media on emerging adults’ prosocial behaviors. The review focuses on studies that observed individuals’ prosocial behavior in real-life settings to eliminate social desirability bias and accurately establish the effects of social media on emerging adults’ prosocial behavior.

stories.headline: Recibir gratitud incrementa la perseverancia y conducta prosocial en niños
stories.finding: En tres experimentos de campo realizados en escuelas, los niños que recibieron agradecimiento mostraron mayores niveles de grit y comportamiento prosocial que aquellos que solo expresaron gratitud. Estos resultados indican que el acto de ser agradecido tiene un efecto positivo más fuerte en la motivación y la interacción social infantil.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que intervenciones que incluyen el reconocimiento de los niños pueden fortalecer su perseverancia y habilidades sociales, ofreciendo una herramienta sencilla para educadores y profesionales de la salud mental que buscan fomentar la resiliencia y el comportamiento prosocial.
stories.paperTitle: Understanding the Impact of Receiving Gratitude and Goal-Oriented Nudges on Children’s Success
stories.journal: Digital Eprints Services at ISB (DESI) (Indian School of Business)
stories.originalAbstract: Introduction This dissertation explores the impact of external factors, specifically receiving gratitude and goal-oriented nudges, on children’s social and academic development. The research contributes to the fields of children’s consumer behavior and behavioral science by examining how external reinforcements shape children's prosocial behavior, perseverance, and performance. The dissertation consists of two essays that employ field experiments to examine the causal effects of gratitude and nudging interventions. Essay 1: Receiving Gratitude enhances Grit and Prosocial Behavior more than Expressing Gratitude Prior research has extensively examined the benefits of expressing gratitude, but little attention has been given to how receiving gratitude (being thanked for helping others) affects the recipient, especially in children. This study investigates whether receiving gratitude fosters higher levels of prosocial behavior, grit, and self-esteem in children compared to merely expressing gratitude. Three field experiments were conducted in school settings. Specifically, Study 1 compared prosocial intent of children receiving gratitude versus those expressing gratitude in a teacher-child interaction. Study 2 examined peer-peer interaction and measured actual prosocial behavior (e.g., willingness to donate or volunteer). In Study 3, a longitudinal design was used to track the long-term effects of receiving gratitude on prosocial behavior, persistence, and self-concept. Findings reveal that being thanked enhances prosocial behavior, increases grit, and strengthens self-esteem, and the role of grit in shaping social behavior. Key Contributions and Implications This study extends gratitude research by demonstrating that receiving gratitude fosters long-term prosocial motivation and persistence, shifting the focus from traditional gratitude interventions that emphasize expressing gratitude. These insights can extend beyond educational to business and management settings, suggesting that fostering a culture of appreciation and recognition has the potential to enhance team cohesion and employee engagement. Essay 2: The Role of Subgoal-Oriented Nudges in Improving Academic Performance This essay examines whether structured subgoal-oriented nudges improve children's academic habits and performance. An eight-month field experiment was conducted with students preparing for a competitive examination to examine the impact of nudging students for completion and submission of assignment on test performance. The experiment was divided into three phases. In the Pre-Nudge Phase assignment submissions were monitored without students being nudged. In the Nudge Phase students received regular goal-oriented nudges encouraging assignment completion and submission along with monitoring of assignments. The final phase was the Post-Nudge Phase where the nudges were withdrawn to assess the persistence effect of the nudge, while monitoring continued. The results indicate that nudges improved test performance, particularly among students with lower self-discipline and lower motivation. However, the effectiveness of nudging varied by gender, with male students benefiting more than female students, raising questions about gendered responses to behavioral interventions. The findings also reveal sustained positive impact of subgoal-oriented nudges, even after the nudges were discontinued. Key Contributions and Implications This study highlights the effectiveness of subgoal-oriented nudges as an intervention to improve performance, which has applications in both education and business contexts. The findings reveal that habit-building mechanisms can be sustained using nudges. In business environments, these findings are suggestive of possible usage of structured nudges for performance tracking, milestone reminders, among others which can enhance employee productivity and facilitate goal completion. The gender differences observed underscore the need for customized strategies, emphasizing gender specific goal-setting approaches in corporate leadership and human resource development. Conclusion By combining insights from children consumer behavior, behavioral science, psychology, and management research, this dissertation provides a deeper understanding of how external reinforcements shape children’s behavior and performance. The findings underscore the power of receiving gratitude and structured nudges in fostering sustained behavioral change, offering actionable strategies that may also be applicable in organizational settings.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué la rumiación prolonga el duelo?
stories.headline: La rumiación del duelo media culpa y trauma
stories.finding: Un estudio longitudinal mostró que la rumiación específica del duelo actúa como mecanismo que vincula la culpa y los asuntos pendientes con síntomas de duelo prolongado y trastorno de estrés postraumático. Así, la rumiación explica la mayor intensidad de estos síntomas a lo largo del tiempo.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que intervenir sobre la rumiación mediante técnicas de mindfulness o reestructuración cognitiva puede prevenir la cronificación del duelo y reducir el riesgo de PTSD, fortaleciendo la resiliencia del doliente.
stories.paperTitle: Guilt and Unfinished Business in Bereavement: Rumination as a Pathway to Prolonged Grief and Trauma
stories.originalAbstract: Background: Bereavement often elicits complex emotional and cognitive reactions, including guilt, unresolved relational concerns, and repetitive negative thinking. Although grief-specific rumination is recognized as a key process that can intensify prolonged grief and trauma-related responses, longitudinal evidence clarifying its mediating role remains limited. This study examines whether grief-specific rumination explains how guilt and unfinished business contribute to prolonged grief and PTSD symptoms over time. Methods: A two-wave longitudinal design was used to assess bereaved adults several months after loss and again at follow-up. Measures included guilt, unfinished business, grief-specific rumination, prolonged grief symptoms, and PTSD symptoms. Mediation analyses tested whether rumination accounted for associations between early loss-related responses (guilt and unfinished business) and psychological outcomes at follow-up. Results: Grief-specific rumination consistently emerged as the mechanism linking guilt and unfinished business with both prolonged grief and PTSD symptoms. These findings suggest that the impact of these early loss-related responses operates primarily through persistent and repetitive cognitive engagement with the loss. Conclusions: Rumination emerged as a central mechanism through which guilt and unfinished business shape bereavement-related distress. These findings highlight the importance of interventions that directly target repetitive negative thinking to promote healthier adjustment following loss.

stories.hook: ¿Qué tipo de ejercicio potencia la función ejecutiva en ADHD?
stories.headline: El ejercicio basado en habilidades supera al aeróbico en inhibición y flexibilidad cognitiva en ADHD
stories.finding: Un meta‑análisis de redes que incluyó 21 ensayos controlados aleatorizados (n = 1 491) mostró que el ejercicio basado en habilidades mejoró significativamente el control inhibitorio (diferencia media estandarizada = 0,73) y la flexibilidad cognitiva (diferencia = 3,08) respecto al ejercicio aeróbico aislado. Además, el ejercicio combinado superó a los controles en la memoria de trabajo (diferencia = 0,73).
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo orienta la prescripción de programas de ejercicio que prioricen actividades basadas en habilidades para potenciar funciones ejecutivas clave en niños y adolescentes con ADHD, ofreciendo una intervención no farmacológica de alta efectividad.
stories.paperTitle: Exercise prescription to improve executive functioning in children and adolescents with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder: a network meta-analysis
stories.originalAbstract: Objective: This study employs a network meta-analysis to investigate the potential effects of exercise type, duration, frequency, intensity, and cycle on executive functions (inhibitory control, working memory, cognitive flexibility) in children and adolescents with ADHD, thereby providing directional insights for future research. Methods: Five databases were systematically searched up to February 1, 2025, yielding 21 RCTs (n = 1,491) involving participants aged 7-18 years. The risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane tools. Standardised mean differences (SMDs) were used as effect measures, while SUCRA was used for probability ranking and GRADE for evidence quality grading. Results: Skill-based exercise outperformed isolated aerobic exercise in inhibitory control (SMD = 0.73, 95% CI 0.31-1.41) and cognitive flexibility (SMD = 3.08, 95% CI 0.52-5.63). Combined exercise outperformed controls in working memory (SMD = 0.73, 95% CI 0.35-1.12). SUCRA ranking indicated the highest cumulative probability for skill-based exercise in inhibitory control (95.8) and cognitive flexibility (95.5), while aerobic exercise had the highest probability for working memory (87.1). Sensitivity analyses indicated that estimates for cognitive flexibility were significantly influenced by individual studies, demonstrating limited robustness. Conclusion: Preliminary evidence suggests that moderate-intensity, skill-based exercise may improve inhibitory control and cognitive flexibility within 6-10 weeks. Aerobic exercise may enhance working memory within 4-5 weeks. However, factors such as ADHD subtypes, age, and dose-response relationships remain unclear. Clinical implementation should be individualised and await high-quality validation.

stories.hook: ¿Qué estilo parental potencia la motivación de los jóvenes deportistas?
stories.headline: Los padres que apoyan la autonomía y moderan su implicación maximizan la motivación deportiva
stories.finding: El análisis de 29 estudios (9 185 atletas y 2 191 padres) mostró que los padres influyen en la motivación deportiva. Los objetivos positivos, un estilo que favorece la autonomía, una implicación moderada, relaciones positivas y un clima de tarea impulsado por los padres son las estrategias óptimas.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo orienta a entrenadores y profesionales a guiar a los padres hacia un apoyo equilibrado, favoreciendo la motivación intrínseca y el bienestar de los jóvenes deportistas, lo que puede mejorar la retención y el rendimiento deportivo.
stories.paperTitle: The role of parents in the motivation of young athletes: a systematic review
stories.originalAbstract: Objectives: Parents are one of the main social agents that shape young athletes' experiences and participation in sports, but they are also the least explored group in the literature. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to conduct a systematic review of research on the role of parents in the motivation of young athletes. Method: The systematic literature review consisted of four electronic databases from which 29 articles published in English and in full-text form in peer-reviewed journals between 1999 and 2023 were retrieved. Results: A total of 29 studies met the eligibility criteria. These studies collectively surveyed 9,185 young athlete participants and 2,191 parent participants. The sample comprised 26 quantitative studies and 3 qualitative studies. The findings underscore that parents play both unique and synergistic multidimensional roles in motivating young athletes. Parents' positive goals and values, autonomy-supportive parenting styles, moderate parental involvement, positive parent-child relationships, and a parent-initiated task climate are identified as optimal parenting strategies. Conclusion: While parents undeniably play a crucial role in motivating young athletes, the manner and extent of their involvement are key.
stories.abstract: Objectives: Parents are one of the main social agents that shape young athletes' experiences and participation in sports, but they are also the least explored group in the literature. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to conduct a systematic review of research on the role of parents in the motivation of young athletes. Method: The systematic literature review consisted of four electronic databases from which 29 articles published in English and in full-text form in peer-reviewed journals between 1999 and 2023 were retrieved. Results: A total of 29 studies met the eligibility criteria. These studies collectively surveyed 9,185 young athlete participants and 2,191 parent participants. The sample comprised 26 quantitative studies and 3 qualitative studies. The findings underscore that parents play both unique and synergistic multidimensional roles in motivating young athletes. Parents' positive goals and values, autonomy-supportive parenting styles, moderate parental involvement, positive parent-child relationships, and a parent-initiated task climate are identified as optimal parenting strategies. Conclusion: While parents undeniably play a crucial role in motivating young athletes, the manner and extent of their involvement are key.

stories.hook: ¿Astrocitos en el PFC son la clave del trastorno depresivo?
stories.headline: Deficiencia de pleiotrofina en astrocitos del PFC desencadena respuestas depresivas
stories.finding: El análisis de núcleos celulares de pacientes con MDD mostró una reducción significativa de astrocitos y una señalización PTN‑PTPRZ1 atenuada en el PFC. En ratones, la reducción de PTN en astrocitos provocó conductas depresivas, que se revertían con suplementación de PTN o sobreexpresión, mediada por la vía AKT.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo identifica la vía PTN‑PTPRZ1‑AKT como un objetivo terapéutico potencial, sugiriendo que moduladores de la señalización astrocitaria podrían restaurar la plasticidad neuronal y aliviar síntomas depresivos.
stories.paperTitle: Astrocytic pleiotrophin deficiency in the prefrontal cortex contributes to stress-induced depressive-like responses in male mice
stories.originalAbstract: Astrocytes are closely linked to depression, and the prefrontal cortex (PFC) is an important brain region involved in major depressive disorder (MDD). However, the underlying mechanism by which astrocytes within PFC contribute to MDD remains unclear. Using single-nucleus RNA sequencing analyses, we show a significant reduction in astrocytes and attenuated pleiotrophin-protein tyrosine phosphatase receptor type Z1 (PTN-PTPRZ1) signaling in astrocyte-to-excitatory neuron communication in the PFC of male MDD patients. We find reduced astrocytes and PTN in the dorsomedial PFC of male mice with depression induced by chronic restraint and social defeat stress. Knockdown of astrocytic PTN induces depression-related responses, which is reversed by exogenous PTN supplementation or overexpression of astrocytic PTN. The antidepressant effects exerted by astrocytic PTN require interaction with PTPRZ1 in excitatory neurons, and PTN-PTPRZ1 activates the AKT signaling pathway to regulate depression-related responses. Our findings indicate the PTN-PTPRZ1-AKT pathway may be a potential therapeutic target for MDD. Astrocytes in the prefrontal cortex are closely linked to depression, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, the authors show that reduction of astrocytic pleiotrophin in the dorsomedial prefrontal cortex contributes to depression-like phenotype in male mice.
